help.intro: Eleven to twenty look irregular but hide one pattern: from thirteen up, you say the unit and then zehn — vier-zehn, acht-zehn — exactly like English 'four-teen'. Only elf (11) and zwölf (12) have to be learnt as words, and two spellings are trimmed: sechzehn drops the s of sechs, siebzehn drops the -en of sieben. Twenty is zwanzig, the first of the tens, and it starts the next block. These teens matter more than they look: ages, times (um vierzehn Uhr), prices and dates all use them constantly.
help.tips[0].title: Unit + zehn
help.tips[0].text: 13 dreizehn, 14 vierzehn, 15 fünfzehn, 18 achtzehn, 19 neunzehn. Say the small number first, then zehn, as one word.
help.tips[0].check.why: The small number comes first, then zehn, all as one word: fünf + zehn = fünfzehn. fünfzig is 50.
help.tips[0].visual.caption: Like English thir-teen: the small number comes first.
help.tips[1].title: The three exceptions
help.tips[1].text: 11 = elf and 12 = zwölf are their own words. 16 = sechzehn (no s: not sechszehn) and 17 = siebzehn (not siebenzehn).
help.tips[1].check.why: Sixteen drops the s of sechs: sechzehn. Likewise siebzehn drops the -en of sieben.
help.tips[1].visual.caption: Two lose a piece; 11 and 12 are their own words.
help.tips[2].title: The 13–19 chant
help.tips[2].text: Chant it with a beat: DREIzehn, VIERzehn, FÜNFzehn, SECHzehn, SIEBzehn, ACHTzehn, NEUNzehn, ZWANzig. The stress is always on the first part.
help.tips[2].check.q: Where is the stress in siebzehn?
help.tips[2].check.why: In the teens the stress always falls on the first part: SIEBzehn, ACHTzehn, NEUNzehn.
help.remember[0]: sechzehn and siebzehn lose a letter or two — the same trim happens in sechzig and siebzig later.
help.remember[1]: The stress is on the unit: VIERzehn, not vierZEHN.
help.context.en: How old are you? – I'm sixteen. My brother is nineteen and my sister is twelve. – And when does school start? – At twenty past eight.
help.mistakes[0].why: Both are shortened; the full words are never used inside a number.
help.mistakes[1].why: Twenty is the first of the tens, not a teen.
help.hook: Learn elf and zwölf, then glue a small number to zehn — the German teens work almost exactly like English.
